claims.claim: The accuracy a converted L-layer network will reach at latency T is predictable, before any spiking simulation, from the trained weights via the cumulative spectral gain G=prod_l||M_l||_2, the active width H, the logit margin, and T.
claims.mechanism: The exact recursion B_hat_l - B_l = (1-alpha) A_hat (E_{l-1} M_l) with E_0=0 gives ||E_L|| ~ ||E_1|| * prod_l||M_l||; the layer-1 error is a sum of independent per-unit quantisation errors, so ||E_1|| ~ sqrt(H)/(2T); a decision flips when the logit perturbation exceeds the margin.
claims.assumptions: No-leak integrate-and-fire with subtractive reset; constant-current layer-1 input; per-unit quantisation errors approximately independent (falsifiable through the sqrt(H) law); the ReLU active-set mask absorbs sign flips, so the norm bound is conservative.
claims.falsifying_ablation: Shuffle the per-unit quantisation errors before propagating them: if the shuffled model predicts gaps as well as the real one, the independence assumption carries no information and the mechanism is unsupported.
claims.split_protocol: Planetoid public split, 20 per class train + 500 validation + 1000 test; 7 seeds; identical hyper-parameter budget for every arm; frozen in experiments/protocol.md.
claims.primary_metric: Mean absolute error in percentage points between predicted and observed conversion gap on held-out (dataset, depth, width, T) cells.
claims.minimum: Spearman rho >= 0.7 between predicted and observed gap over held-out cells.
claims.expected_strong: MAE <= 1.0 pp on held-out cells and predicted required-T exact on >= 70% of cells, with no error larger than one grid step.
claims.failure: MAE > 2.0 pp, or required-T exact on < 50% of cells; the predictive claim then leaves the title and the laws are reported as descriptive.
claims.simple_baseline: Predict each dataset's mean gap at that T, ignoring architecture (constant-per-latency predictor).
claims.strong_baseline: Predict from the ANN's validation accuracy alone, assuming the gap is a fixed function of dataset and T.
claims.matched_control: The same predictor fitted on the same number of cells with G replaced by a random draw of the same distribution, so any gain is not the fit's degrees of freedom.
claims.implementation_path: experiments/core.py supplies G, H, B_l and margins; experiments/wp7_predict.py performs leave-one-config-out and leave-one-dataset-out fitting and scoring.
claims.prototype_check: Reproduce the published amplification exponent 0.948 from the nine already-measured depth cells before any new grid is run.
claims.calibration_evidence: results/wp3_depth.json gives exponent 0.948 at r=0.990 over nine cells, and ||E_1||/sqrt(H) stable at 1.72 down to 1.61 over H=16..128.
claims.test_isolation: No cell contributes to both fit and evaluation; each T is excluded from its own fit set; fitting uses train/validation statistics only and never test labels.
claims.stop_return_condition: If the grid cannot finish within 24 h wall clock, cut widths to {16,64} keeping 7 seeds; if MAE still exceeds 2 pp, return to guidance before experiments rather than train toward the target.

claims.claim: Under one protocol and at T <= 4 the conversion is not Pareto-dominated in accuracy versus synaptic operations by three published spiking-GNN formulations.
claims.mechanism: Conversion discretises an already-trained computation: it pays no per-latency training cost and inherits the ANN's features, whereas a directly trained spiking network learns sparser but weaker layer-1 features at low T.
claims.assumptions: The three arms are re-implemented faithfully enough to be comparable; SOPs = T * edges * active_hidden is an acceptable energy proxy; published numbers are not reproduced because no checkpoints exist.
claims.falsifying_ablation: Repeat the Pareto with the conversion arm trained at one T and evaluated on all others (its actual deployment mode); if the advantage disappears it was a tuning artefact, not a property of conversion.
claims.split_protocol: Same as claim P, plus the ogbn-arxiv official time split for the scale row; every arm shares split, seeds and hyper-parameter budget.
claims.primary_metric: Number of graphs on which some conversion point at T <= 4 is dominated (lower accuracy and higher SOPs) by an external arm.
claims.minimum: No external arm dominates the conversion at T <= 4 on more than one graph.
claims.expected_strong: Conversion reaches ANN-1.5 pp with strictly fewer SOPs than every external arm on at least two of the three citation graphs.
claims.failure: An external arm has both higher accuracy and lower SOPs at T <= 4 on two or more graphs; section 4.2 is then rewritten as a training-cost trade and the low-latency claim is withdrawn.
claims.simple_baseline: Rate-coded (Poisson) spiking GCN of the published SpikingGCN formulation.
claims.strong_baseline: Directly trained spiking GCN with surrogate-gradient BPTT and per-step dropout, plus the SpikingGCN architecture (SGC-2 propagation with a 512-wide spiking layer).
claims.matched_control: The same two-layer GCN trained as an ANN and converted: identical width, depth and data.
claims.implementation_path: protocols/baselines_published.py for the direct and Poisson arms; protocols/spikinggcn_baseline.py for the published architecture.
claims.prototype_check: Confirm all three arms reproduce their stored seven-seed means to within 0.01 pp before extending the grid to T=32.
claims.calibration_evidence: Measured: conversion 0.8046/0.6907/0.7771, direct 0.7920/0.6646/0.7751, SpikingGCN-architecture 0.8169/0.7073/0.7603 on Cora/CiteSeer/PubMed at each arm's best T.
claims.test_isolation: Early stopping and bias calibration use train/validation masks only; test labels are read once per run for the reported number.
claims.stop_return_condition: If any arm misses the prototype check by more than 0.1 pp, stop and diagnose before extending the grid; never publish a Pareto whose arms were not re-validated.

claims.claim: The membrane readout is exactly invariant to the temporal order of upstream spikes, while the integer-count readout is not.
claims.mechanism: The output accumulator is sum_t inst_t = A_hat (count_1 M_2) + T b_2, which contains no t; the count decoder depends on when the running sum crosses theta, so it does see the order.
claims.assumptions: No-leak integrate-and-fire with subtractive reset; the decoder reads the un-reset accumulator; layer-1 input is constant, so its spike train can be reordered offline without touching anything upstream.
claims.falsifying_ablation: Replace the sum readout with a leaky membrane (decay != 1): order should then matter, and if it still does not, the invariance is a simulator artefact rather than a property of the decoder.
claims.split_protocol: Same as claim P; two graphs, both neuron models, four perturbation cells, 7 seeds.
claims.primary_metric: Spread (max minus min) of test accuracy in percentage points across the four temporal perturbations, for the membrane decoder.
claims.expected_strong: Membrane spread <= 0.01 pp on both graphs and both neuron models, with count spread >= 0.3 pp in the same cells.
claims.failure: Membrane spread > 0.1 pp, which would falsify the accumulator identity as implemented.
claims.simple_baseline: Integer-count readout, the field's default decoder.
claims.strong_baseline: TPP stochastic neuron from the 2025 cross-layer misalignment work, where order is expected to matter for both decoders.
claims.matched_control: The unperturbed spike train (base cell) for each dataset and neuron, so every spread is measured against its own control.
claims.prototype_check: Confirm on one seed that permuting the layer-1 train leaves the membrane accuracy unchanged bit for bit.
claims.calibration_evidence: Measured spread 0.000 pp in all four membrane cells and 0.386-1.614 pp in the count cells.
claims.test_isolation: Only the spike train is perturbed; weights, masks and theta are untouched, so order is the single changed variable.
claims.stop_return_condition: If the leaky-membrane ablation shows order still does not matter, drop the order language entirely and describe the decoder only by its quantisation behaviour.
